articles.name: Adding Your 10Web Domain to 10Web Hosted Sites
articles.title: Adding Your 10Web Domain to 10Web Hosted Sites
articles.body:
If you've purchased a domain through 10Web, linking it with your 10Web-hosted website is a simple process. This is all done within 10Web's unified hosting system, eliminating the need for manual DNS management.

Linking your domain

  1. Click the Manage button next to the site you want to link your domain to.
  2. Go to the Domains menu.
  3. Click on the Add Domain button.

You'll encounter three options to choose from:

  • From Domain List: If you've previously purchased the domain from 10Web, you'll find it listed here. Simply select the domain you want to link and proceed.
  • Get a New Domain: Use this option if you haven't bought the domain yet. Enter the desired domain name and complete the purchase process. You can read more details about it in the Domain Pricing and Renewal Models article.
  • Already Have a Domain: This option isn't covered in this article as it pertains to domains purchased from third-party registrars. If this applies to you, refer to the article on how to point a third-party domain to a 10Web Hosted site.

Once you've added your 10Web domain to your hosted site, no further action is required for domain pointing, as everything is handled automatically.

Note:

You might need to wait a bit for the DNS records to be resolved. You can use DNS Checker to regularly check whether your domain records are resolved or not.

After the records are resolved, make the domain primary for your site to load under your domain name.

Note:

10Web offers free SSL for hosted websites. When pointing to your domain, the free SSL option is checked to be added by default. If after making the domain primary, you notice that the site is not secure, enter Hosting Services > Tools > SSL Certificate and Generate a free SSL certificate.

For integrating email hosting or other services with your domain, you may need to add DNS records, which can be easily done from the Domain > Manage DNS section. Refer to the DNS Records article for more accurate details.

articles.name: Pointing Your 10Web-Purchased Domain to Another Host
articles.title: Pointing Your 10Web-Purchased Domain to Another Host
articles.body:
After purchasing a domain through 10Web, you might decide to host your website with a third-party provider. To do this, you can point your domain using either Nameserver (NS) or A records. This guide includes both methods for pointing the domain.

Note:

If you don’t have a domain name yet, you can follow this guide to purchase one.

Step 1: Locating domain and DNS settings

To locate your domain and DNS settings:

  1. In the 10Web Dashboard go to My Products > Domains.
  2. You will be automatically redirected to the Domains portfolio.
  3. Click on your domain name. You will be redirected to the Overview section.
  4. Select the DNS tab for pointing with A / CNAME record or select the Nameservers tab to point with nameservers.

Note:

You can locate the DNS using the three dots (more options) beside your domain data. Here, you can directly access the Manage DNS, Manage Nameservers and Manage Domain sections.

Step 2: Pointing a domain

There are two ways to point your domain: Nameservers or A record.

A record is used to link a domain name (e.g. example.com) to an IPv4 address.

Nameservers are the servers where all DNS records are managed. To manage your DNS records in the 10Web dashboard, you will need to point your domain using the 10Web nameservers.

Note:

It can take up to 24 hours for the newly added records to be resolved and changes to take effect. You can use DNS Checker to periodically check the status.

Option1: Pointing with Custom Nameservers

To point your domain with nameservers to your 3rd party-hosted website follow these steps:

  1. Navigate to the Nameservers section of your domain.
  2. Click on the Edit button.
  3. Choose Custom Nameserver.
  4. Enter the nameservers provided by your host. Typically, you will get 2 fields to add your custom nameservers, if you need more, click on + Add nameserver button.
  5. Save your changes.

Important:

After switching your nameservers to Custom nameservers, 10Web can no longer manage or update DNS records for you. Use the DNS management interface provided by your hosting company to add new records or edit existing ones.

Option 2: Pointing with A and CNAME Records

If you want to use 10Web nameservers, you can still point your domain to 3rd party hosting by just creating A and CNAME records.
For this, access the DNS section, found either through the domain's DNS tab or the more options menu next to your domain in the list.

Add an A record

  1. Click Add DNS Record > Add New
  2. Select A as the record type.
  3. Leave the Hostname field empty to apply this record to your root domain.
  4. In the IPv4 Address field, type the IP address of your hosting server.
  5. Leave the TTL as default unless you have a specific need to adjust it.
  6. Click Add Record.

Add a CNAME record for www redirection

  1. Click Add DNS Record and choose Add New from the dropdown list.
  2. Choose CNAME as the record type.
  3. For the Hostname field, enter www
  4. In the Server field, input your root domain (e.g., "domain.com").
  5. Leave the TTL as default unless you have a specific need to adjust it.
  6. Click Add Record.

Important:

You can point your domain using A record and CNAME only if you are using the Default nameservers provided by 10Web.

Note:

If your domain is successfully pointed but you encounter issues with your website, you need to reach out to your hosting provider for further assistance.

articles.name: Domain Pricing and Renewal Models
articles.title: Domain Pricing and Renewal Models
articles.body:
This guide focuses on the pricing models for domain purchases and the domain renewal process, ensuring you have all the information needed to manage your domain subscription effectively.

Intro to domain subscriptions

Pricing varies based on the domain name chosen. This flexibility allows you to find a domain that fits your budget and brand.

Note:

Currently, you can purchase a domain only if you already have an active 10Web Platform plan.

Each domain purchased creates a domain agreement separate from your platform plans and other domain subscriptions. This allows independent management of all domain subscriptions, including renewal and cancellation processes.

Important:

If you decide to cancel your hosting subscription with 10Web, your domain subscription remains active. Each domain subscription should be canceled separately.

As of now, domains can only be purchased with an annual renewal model; however, more flexible options are on the roadmap.

Note:

Even if your main platform subscription is set to monthly payments, domain subscription payments will be set to annual renewal.

You can enable or disable Auto-renewal directly from the Domains menu of your 10Web Dashboard. The renewal price for your domain will be visible next to the Auto-renewal setting, giving you a clear view of future billing.

Note:

Renewal prices are subject to change. We advise revisiting the pricing information as your domain's renewal date approaches to confirm the exact amount.

How to purchase a domain

10Web offers a streamlined process for purchasing and managing domains directly from our platform.

To find your domain, you need to access the domain management interface:

  1. On 10Web Dashboard navigate to the top bar where you’ll find the My Products menu item.
  2. Click on My Products > Domains submenu to access our domain services.
  3. By default, you will be taken to the Get a New Domain section. Use the Search bar to choose your desired domain name.
  4. Once you’ve found your desired domain name, click on Get it button.
  5. On the checkout page, you'll be prompted to fill in or confirm your billing information.
  6. Add/choose your preferred payment method.
  7. Complete your domain purchase with Secure Checkout.

Important:

If you adjust your billing details on the checkout page, these changes will apply to your entire 10Web account, affecting all products and services linked to it.

After successful payment, your domain will be listed under Domains Portfolio section where you can manage settings like domain privacy, DNS, contact information, and more. 

How to cancel a domain

Canceling your domain subscription is simple and can be done directly from your 10Web Dashboard:

  1. On 10Web Dashboard navigate to the top bar where you’ll find the My Products menu item.
  2. Click on My Products > Domains submenu to access our domain services.
  3. Toggle off the Auto-renewal button next to the desired domain name.

This will prevent the domain from automatically renewing at the end of its subscription period.

Transferring your domain to another registrar

You can transfer your domain name from 10Web to another domain registrar. However, please note that newly registered domains have a mandatory 60-day transfer lock period imposed by ICANN regulations. During this period, we are unable to initiate the transfer process.

Once the 60-day period has elapsed from the date of your domain purchase:

  1. Contact our customer support team to request a transfer authorization code (EPP code).
  2. Use this code to initiate the transfer process with the new registrar.

Note:

Note: For .co.uk domains, please, provide us the registrar tag from your new domain registrar to confirm the transfer.

Important:

Make you your domain subscription is cancelled on 10Web Dashboard not to be charged at the end of the subscription period.

articles.name: The Finder
articles.title: The Finder
articles.body:
The Finder tool is a dynamic and efficient way to navigate through your website's backend, 10Web Website Builder, and even the front end with ease. This feature is designed to enhance your workflow, allowing you to quickly search and access different parts of your site, settings, and content without the need to navigate through multiple menus.

Accessing the Finder

To launch the Finder, you can do so from anywhere on your site: while in the 10Web Website Builder, the WordPress admin dashboard, or viewing the front end of your site Press CMD / CTRL + E to open the Finder.

Type in what you're looking for - be it to navigate, create, or edit content - and hit enter. You'll be directed to your desired location instantly.

Ways to enhance your workflow with the Finder

Create New Content: Use Finder to start new posts, pages, custom post types, templates, etc.
Edit Existing Content: Quickly find and edit any content on your site, such as posts, pages, or templates.
Navigate 10Web Builder Screens: Easily switch between the builder editor and various 10Web Builder settings pages.

articles.name: Configuring the Dimensions and Dynamics of Flexbox Containers
articles.title: Configuring the Dimensions and Dynamics of Flexbox Containers
articles.body:
Containers are integral in 10Web Website Builder for organizing widgets, crafting templates, and ensuring a consistent design across your website. Knowing how to effectively manage the size and behavior of your containers is key to efficient web design.

Setting container dimensions

To modify a container's dimensions:

  1. Select the desired container
  2. Open the Layout tab
  3. Go to the Container settings section
  • Content width: Choose between Boxed or Full Width. Boxed allows you to define the width inside the container, while Full Width ensures content extends across the entire space of the container.
  • Min height: This setting is crucial for guaranteeing visibility, especially in mobile layouts.

Adjust height and width with units like pixels, percentages, or viewport dimensions, selectable in the top-right corner of each setting. Learn more about the units of measurement here.

Item dynamics

Below the sizing options, you'll find settings that govern item dynamics within the container, such as direction, justification, alignment, item gaps, and wrapping behavior.

Additional options

Tailor the container's behavior with Overflow settings and HTML tag selection.

Overflow

  • Default: Items that go beyond the container's size are visible.
  • Hidden: Content that spills over is hidden.
  • Auto: Introduces a scrollbar for any content exceeding the container's bounds.

HTML tag customization

Assign an appropriate HTML tag from the dropdown to encapsulate your container, which is a pivotal consideration for SEO and the content's importance within the DOM hierarchy.

Note:

You can set responsive-specific HTML tags as needed.

articles.name: Role Manager
articles.title: Role Manager
articles.body:
With Role Manager, you can assign specific roles to users based on the access level you want them to have. This function allows you to either block certain users from accessing 10Web Builder editor or let them edit content only. This way, you can minimize accidents and secure your design.

User roles on WordPress

By default, WordPress comes with five pre-defined user roles. Every user role has its own set of permissions. For example, the Subscriber role on WordPress allows users to view content, comment on posts, and manage their profile. As you move up the roles, each one has more permissions than the last.
Certain plugins or themes can introduce new roles with unique functions or adjust existing ones. You also have the option to use a plugin to customize the capabilities associated with each role according to your needs.

Administrator: Administrators have full control over the site, allowing them to delete posts and pages, activate and install plugins, and perform other crucial actions. In a single-site setup, they can also remove everything, underscoring the need for trust in assigning this role.
Editor: Editors have the authority to handle and upload all types of site content, such as posts and pages.
Author: Authors can only create and remove their own posts but cannot modify pages.
Contributor: Contributors are able to compose posts, however, their submissions need approval from those with higher permissions.
Subscriber: Subscribers have a limited role, primarily able to manage their own profile settings. They lack permission to edit, publish, or contribute content to the site.

Applying and editing WordPress user roles

If you want to add users and set their roles:

  1. On your WordPress Dashboard click on Users and select Add New to add a new user.
  2. In the provided fields, input the new user's email, username, and any additional details you have.
  3. Choose to either let WordPress auto-generate a password or create one yourself. Decide if you want to email this password to the new user.
  4. From the dropdown menu, pick the role you want to assign to the new user.
  5. Click on Add New User to complete the process.

To Modify Existing Users' Roles:

  1. Navigate to Users and then All Users.
  2. Click on the user whose role you wish to change.
  3. Find the Role section, and select the new role from the dropdown menu.
  4. Click Update User to apply the changes.

10Web Builder Role Manager

Role Manager limits clients from editing sensitive parts of a website’s design while editing the content. It seamlessly works with WordPress's built-in user roles and those added by themes or plugins, enhancing your site's security and usability.

Here's how to use it:

  1. Login into the WordPress Dashboard of your website.
  2. Find and select Elementor from the menu options.
  3. Within the Elementor menu, click on Role Manager. This is where you can manage and set permissions for different user roles.
  4. Set Permissions:
    No Access to Editor: Selecting this will prevent the chosen user roles from accessing the 10Web Builder Editor.
    Enable JSON File Uploads: This allows specified roles to edit text and images by uploading JSON files, which lets them manage content without changing the website’s layout.
    Enable the option to use the HTML widget: The option allows users with that specific role to utilize HTML widgets within the Elementor page builder plugin.
  5. Make sure to save your changes to ensure the new permissions are applied to user roles.

If you don't select either of these checkboxes for the role, they will possess unrestricted access to Elementor. Therefore, ensure you select at least one of the settings for roles you wish to limit.

By integrating these controls, Role Manager provides a flexible and secure way to manage your site's user roles, combining ease of use with powerful customization options.

articles.name: Configuring Page Settings
articles.title: Configuring Page Settings
articles.body:
Page Settings in 10Web Website Builder are essential for customizing the basic aspects of your webpage, including naming your page, selecting a featured image, and setting up a background. This feature provides control over how your page appears and functions, ensuring it meets your specific needs and preferences.

Accessing and configuring page settings

  1. Select the gear icon situated at the top
  2. Navigate to the Settings tab
  3. Open the General Settings section

In the Page settings menu you will see 3 tabs:

Settings tab

In the Settings tab, you can manage the following:

Note:

The appearance and available options may vary depending on the page type.

  • Title: Customize the page title.
  • Status: Change the publishing state using the dropdown menu. Options include Draft, Pending Review, Private, and Published.
  • Excerpt: Enter a brief summary of the page, useful for archive pages.
  • Featured image: Add an image to represent your page, enhancing SEO and visibility in search results.
  • Order:  Assign a numerical order to the page, aiding in page hierarchy organization.
  • Allow Comments: Toggle to enable visitor comments for engagement.
  • Hide Title:  Toggle the option to display or conceal the page title.
  • Page Layout: Choose the page display style (Default, Elementor Canvas, Elementor Full Width, Theme) via the dropdown menu.

Style tab

In the Style tab, you can adjust:

  • Margin and Padding: Control the layout spacing. See the Padding and Margins article for details.
  • Background Type: Set a color, image, or video background. 

Advanced tab

The Advanced Tab offers the following options to manage:

  • Custom CSS: Add personalized CSS code to your page
  • Custom HTML: Add your own custom HTML or JavaScript here.

These settings offer a comprehensive approach to customizing your page, from aesthetic choices like background and layout to functional aspects like visibility status and visitor interactions.

articles.name: History: Actions and Revisions
articles.title: History: Actions and Revisions
articles.body:
10Web Builder offers advanced editing features, including Revision History, Undo, and Redo, allowing for precise control over website edits.

You can access these options through the History Panel, located at the top left of your page. The History Panel is split into Actions and Revisions tabs for detailed tracking of every edit.

Actions tab 

Within 10Web Builder, the Actions Tab precisely records each action performed by you. Navigating and selecting from the list of Actions enables you to retrace your steps, allowing you to navigate backward and forward through your actions.

Each action listed shows what part of the page you changed and how you changed it. At the bottom of this list, Editing started indicates the time you began your edits. For a deeper dive into the history, you can move over to the Revisions Tab.

Revisions tab 

Whenever you update a page, it saves a new version of it. Each saved version shows when it was created and who created it. To access previous versions, simply click on the desired version for a preview. To utilize a selected version, click the Apply button. Conversely, if you wish to go back to current version, click on the Discard button.

Undo / Redo Keyboard Shortcuts: To undo your last change, use CTRL-Z (on Windows) or CMD-Z (on Mac). To redo it, use CTRL-SHIFT-Z or CMD-SHIFT-Z.

articles.name: Accessing and Using Navigator in 10Web Website Builder
articles.title: Accessing and Using Navigator in 10Web Website Builder
articles.body:
The Navigator is a vital tool that provides quick access to all elements in the editor with a single click. It’s especially useful for navigating long pages or complex layouts, handling elements like Z-Index, minus margins, or absolute positioning. This feature makes it easy to find and edit hidden elements, improving your design workflow.

How to access the Navigator

There are several ways of accessing the Navigator while editing your pages:

  • Direct Selection: Right-click any element on your page and select Structure from the menu. This action will pinpoint the element within the navigation tree.
  • Using the Editor Top Panel: Click on the Structure button located at the top of the panel.
  • Keyboard Shortcut: Press Cmd/Ctrl + I to open the Navigator instantly.

Navigating and editing with the Navigator

Once you've accessed the Navigator, a variety of settings and actions are at your disposal:

    • Edit Elements: Simply click on any element within the Navigator to be taken to its Edit panel for immediate modifications.
    • Rearrange Elements: Drag and drop elements within the tree to reposition them on your page.
    • Access Right-Click Options: Right-clicking an element within the Navigator opens a menu for quick actions like Edit, Duplicate, Copy, and Paste.
  • Hide/Show Elements: Use the View button beside an element to toggle its visibility. This action only affects your view in the editor, not the live website.
  • Rename Elements: Double-click an element's name and type in a custom identifier for easier reference.
  • Collapse/Expand Elements: Manage your view of the tree by collapsing or expanding individual elements or all elements at once using the arrow buttons.

Customizing the Navigator's position

  • Floating Mode: You can move the Navigator panel freely around your workspace to suit your design process.
  • Docking Mode: Secure the Navigator to the side of your screen by dragging it towards the right side until a vertical drop zone appears, then release.

The Navigator is an essential tool within 10Web Website Builder, designed to enhance your website-building experience by providing streamlined navigation and editing capabilities. By leveraging these features, you can efficiently manage even the most complex designs, ensuring a smooth and productive workflow.

articles.name: Typography
articles.title: Typography
articles.body:
Typography plays a pivotal role in website building, acting as a bridge between design aesthetics and user readability. Typography ensures that content is not only visually pleasing but also clear and legible.

To start editing the typography of your website elements, open the Style tab of the widget and click on the edit icon located in front of Typography.

Family

Family refers to the kind of Typeface or the type of design of a font. For example, Times New Roman is a font family type.

To choose a font family:

  1. Click on the drop-down menu in front of Family
  2. Choose the font type you want to use

Size

The size refers to the size of your font. You can set the Font Size using any of the measurement types by clicking the measurement type on top of the number field. By default, the measurement type is set to pixels.

To customize the size:

  1. Move the dot on the slider to either side or
  2. Enter a number value in the number field

Weight

This setting changes the thickness of the letters. To customize the Weight of your font, click on the drop-down arrow in front of Weight and choose from any of the options.

Transform

The Transform function enables the conversion between lower case to upper case and vice versa, or to capitalize the first letters of sentences. To use the Transform function, click on the drop-down menu and choose from the list.

Style

Allows the option of enabling or disabling italics. This includes the possibility for oblique text, a variant of italics suited for specific fonts. Use the drop-down menu to choose from the options.

Decoration

Option to underline, overline, or line through the text.

Line height

Use this option to adjust the spacing between your sentences. You can set the spacing in pixels, EM or REM. Use the bar to adjust the height or enter a numeric value in the number field.

Letter spacing

When your text alignment seems off, tweak the distance between characters using Letter Spacing. This is quantifiable in pixels, EM. Use the bar to adjust the spacing or set a numeric value in the number field.

Word spacing

Word spacing is usually used for fine-tuning the page layouts. This too is measured in either pixels, EM or REM. Use the bar to adjust the spacing or enter a numeric value in the number field.

Note:

You can adjust the size, line height, letter spacing and word spacing for different devices by clicking the device icon located in front of them.

articles.name: Intro to Flexbox Containers
articles.title: Intro to Flexbox Containers
articles.body:
10Web Website Builder uses Flexbox containers to organize webpages, offering greater efficiency than sections, columns, and inner sections. Containers hold page elements like widgets and other containers, and when placed inside another, they become nested or child containers.

There are principally two container categories:

  • Grid containers: Designed with symmetrical row-column layouts, and
  • Flexbox containers: Offer asymmetrical design layouts.

Flexbox containers offer a plethora of creative liberties and boosts design efficiency.

Optimized web page performance

One of the pronounced benefits of containers is the enhanced page performance. Unlike the dual wrapper elements in sections and columns, containers have just one. This streamlined structure effectively reduces the DOM (Document Object Model) size, potentially enhancing the performance of your web page when implemented correctly.

Design freedom

When you nest child containers within parent ones, you gain unmatched control over direction, alignment, order, length, and positioning of 10Web widgets. Plus, there's no need for extra sections or columns, making the process seamless.

Resilient web design

10Web containers empower designers with the agility to rearrange web page components. This ensures consistent element arrangement across varying screen dimensions, delivering a superior user experience.

Multipurpose web elements

Boost your design workflow with 10Web container's feature to repurpose web elements. Design a container, populate it with your desired elements, save, and redeploy it wherever needed, saving time and ensuring consistency.

The introduction of containers in 10Web Website Builder signifies a new era of web design capabilities, maximizing 10Web Builder’s potential.

What’s next

Now that you've grasped the power of Flexbox Containers, you’ll need to learn how to create containers to further enhance your understanding.

articles.name: Understanding Margins and Padding
articles.title: Understanding Margins and Padding
articles.body:
Web design often involves intricate details that define the look and feel of a webpage. Two of these essential details are margins and padding.

Margins

Margins determine the space outside an element, effectively creating a gap between it and surrounding elements. Think of it as the outer boundary of your element, separating it from others.

Padding

Padding, on the other hand, is the space inside an element's border. It determines the distance between the content of the element and its border, offering room for the content to breathe and ensuring it doesn't feel cramped.

Applying margins

Directional control

You can adjust margins individually for the top, bottom, left, or right side of an element or the container itself. This ability offers precise control, allowing designers to position elements perfectly within a container.

Negative margins

A lesser-known trick in web design is the use of negative margins. When combined with properties like z-index, negative margins can enable elements to stack or overlap. For instance, if you want a section to visually cover another, applying a top negative margin would achieve this effect.

Applying paddings

Containers

Padding is pivotal in ensuring that elements within containers have sufficient space around them. Applying a percentage-based padding, say 5% on the top and bottom of a container, can significantly enhance visual appeal, making content more readable and engaging.

Internal adjustments

Besides spacing out content from the borders, padding can also be used to control the visual space within containers, ensuring a balanced look.

How to locate and adjust settings

Advanced settings

Typically, general padding and margin settings for elements are located under the Advanced tab of the widget or container in 10Web website builder.

Additional padding settings

Widgets, such as buttons and forms, may have extra settings located under the Style tab, allowing for more granular adjustments.

Global settings

The Site Settings usually house default values for container paddings. It's worth noting that any settings made on the container itself would override these defaults.
You can access the default value for the container’s padding from Layout Settings.

Measurement units

When setting values for margins and padding, designers have multiple units at their disposal, including PX, EM, %, and REM. A handy feature in many design tools is the chain icon, which when clicked, can unlink values, allowing for individual adjustments.

articles.name: How to Add a Background Slideshow
articles.title: How to Add a Background Slideshow
articles.body:
In 10Web Website Builder, you have the capability to craft dynamic backgrounds for containers by setting up a slideshow of images. This allows for intricate designs and layouts with smooth transition effects to add visual interest.

Adding a background slideshow

To configure a background slideshow:

  1. Edit your page/website with the 10Web Builder
  2. Click on the desired container
  3. Click on the Style tab
  4. Navigate to the Background type
  5. Click on the Slideshow icon

Configuring the slideshow background

  • Add images: Click Add Images to select which images you want in the slideshow. After selection, confirm by clicking Create a New Gallery > Insert Gallery.
  • Infinite loop: Toggle to YES to cycle the slideshow without end.
  • Duration: Set how long each slide is displayed, measured in milliseconds.
  • Transition: Select the transition effect for slides, options include Fade, Slide Right, Slide Left, Slide Down, or Slide Up.
  • Transition duration: Determine the transition speed between slides in milliseconds.
  • Background size: Decide the size of the background images, with choices like Default, Auto, Cover, or Contain.
  • Background position: Pick the focal point for the background image from options such as Default, Top Left, Top Center, Top Right, Center Left, Center Center, Center Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Center, or Bottom Right.
  • Lazyload: Toggle this option to ON to improve page load speeds by loading images only as they become visible to the user.
  • Ken Burns effect: Activate this to apply a subtle zoom and panning effect to your background images.
  • Direction (Ken Burns Effect): If the Ken Burns Effect is enabled, select whether the zoom direction should be In or Out.

articles.name: Global Colors
articles.title: Global Colors
articles.body:
Global Colors is a feature within 10web Builder that allows users to define a set of color options that can be easily reused throughout the website. Instead of manually specifying colors each time they're needed, users can create a palette of global colors, which can then be applied consistently across various elements such as text, backgrounds, buttons, and more.

How to access global colors

To review and adjust your global colors:

  1. Open 10Web Editor and click on the Site Settings icon located on the left of the top bar.
  2. Under Design System click Global colors.

Default color settings

In 10Web Website Builder, default color settings play distinct roles in the design of your website:

  • Primary colors: Typically applied to headings and icons.
  • Secondary colors: Often used for list items, subheadings, animated headings, and the backgrounds of price tables.
  • Text colors: The default for paragraphs and menu items.
  • Accent colors: Used to highlight links, button backgrounds, tab and accordion headings, and badges.
  • Inverse primary: Refers to a color that contrasts with the primary color and is suitable for use on light backgrounds.
  • Custom Colors: Used to add new global colors.

How to add new global color

To introduce a new color to your palette:

  1. Click on Add Color.
  2. Enter a name and desired shade.
  3. Click on the Save Changes button.

How to edit global colors

To customize your global colors:

  • Modify a color: Simply hover over a color swatch and click it to open the color picker, where you can select a new hue.
  • Reorder colors: Click the arrow icon to rearrange the global colors.
  • Delete a color: Click the delete icon to remove a color.

Note:

System colors cannot be deleted.

  • Rename a color: Click on the color name to edit it, and type in the new designation.

Remember to save your changes after making adjustments.

articles.name: Containers in 10Web Builder: Flexible Element Positioning
articles.title: Containers in 10Web Builder: Flexible Element Positioning
articles.body:
10Web Website Builder offers flexible controls for arranging elements within containers. Here's a breakdown of the available options to help you customize your layouts:

Navigate to the Items section under the Layout tab to access these controls.

Direction

The Direction setting lets you decide the arrangement in which the elements within your container will be showcased.

  • Row: Elements are oriented horizontally.
  • Column: Elements stand vertically.
  • Row-reversed: Elements are displayed horizontally but in the opposite sequence.
  • Column-reversed: Elements are set vertically, but the order is inverted.

Justify content

The Justify Content setting controls the alignment of elements along the main axis, which is determined by the container's chosen Direction.

  • Start: Elements align to the left side of the container (if the Direction is set to Row) or the top of the container (if the Direction is set to Column).
  • Center: Elements are positioned in the center of the container.
  • End: Elements align to the right side of the container (if the Direction is set to Row) or the bottom of the container (if the Direction is set to Column).
  • Space Between: This option distributes equal spacing between all the elements within the container, from the first to the last.
  • Space Around: Similar to Space Between, but it also adds extra spacing at the beginning and end of the container, creating a margin around the elements.
  • Space Evenly: This option ensures uniform spacing between all elements, including the container's edges. This can be useful for creating a grid-like layout.

Align items

Align Items aids in determining the alignment of elements along their cross-axis, based on the choice made in the Direction option.

  • Start: Elements align to the top of the container (if the Direction is set to Row) or to the left of the container (if the Direction is set to Column).
  • Center: Elements centrally align within the container.
  • End: Elements positioned at the bottom of the container (if the Direction is set to Row) or at the right of the container (if the Direction is set to Column).
  • Stretch: Elements expand to span the entire container height or width (depending on the Direction setting).

Gaps

Here, you can adjust the spacing between individual elements, be it widgets or other containers. The units available are pixels (PX), percentages (%), or Viewport Width (VW).

Note:

The default gap between elements is 20PX. However, this can be modified by heading to Site Settings Layout.

Wrap

The Wrap feature determines if the elements inside will stay confined to a single row or if they overflow to subsequent rows.

  • No Wrap: All elements are constrained to a single horizontal line.
  • Wrap: If items exceed the container's width, they transition to the next line.

Important:

The Align Items and Justify Content settings work together to give you precise control over element positioning within a container. The Direction setting determines the main and cross axes, which in turn establish the behavior of these alignment properties.

Note:

Dive deeper into options related to organizing elements within containers by checking out the Advanced tab.

articles.name: Understanding and Using Shadows in 10Web Builder
articles.title: Understanding and Using Shadows in 10Web Builder
articles.body:
Shadows are a subtle but powerful design tool that can add depth, dimension, and visual interest to your creations. 10Web builder offers two main types of shadows:

  • Box Shadow: Creates a box-like border with a shadow, making an element appear raised. This is the type of shadow typically found under Border or Box Shadow settings for containers, elements, and individual widgets.
  • Text Shadow: Adds a shadow behind text to enhance readability or create a stylized look.

Where to find Shadow settings

10Web Builder offers flexible shadow controls that are integrated into the design workflow. Here's a general guide on where you'll usually find shadow settings for different element types:

  • Containers, Sections & Columns: Look for shadow options within the Style tab, typically under the Border or Box Shadow sections.
  • Images, Buttons, and Other Widgets: Many individual widgets have dedicated Box Shadow settings directly within the Style tab.
  • Text Elements (Headings, Text Editors, etc.): Dedicated Text Shadow controls are usually found within the Style tab.

Important:

The exact location and naming of shadow settings might slightly vary depending on the specific widget or element you're working with.

Customizing your Shadows

Once you've located the shadow settings, here's what you can adjust:

  • Color: Choose the perfect shadow color to complement your design.
  • Horizontal & Vertical: Control the direction of the shadow, simulating different light sources.
  • Blur: Soften the edges of the shadow for a diffused look or keep it sharp for a crisp effect.
  • Spread: Increase or decrease the overall size of the shadow.
  • Position: Choose Outline for a shadow that falls outside the element, or Inset for a shadow that appears within its borders.

Quick tip:

  • Boxed Shadows are perfect for making buttons or sections look like they're raised off the page.
  • Text Shadows should be used subtly to improve readability, especially on busy backgrounds.
  • Don't be afraid to experiment! Shadows are versatile tools; play around to see what effects work best for your design.

articles.name: Deactivating Flexbox Containers
articles.title: Deactivating Flexbox Containers
articles.body:
10Web Builder utilizes containers to structure page layouts. While this modern approach enhances design flexibility, some users may prefer the traditional sections-based layout due to familiarity or existing website structures. This guide outlines how to switch off the container feature for users who wish to work with sections instead.

How to deactivate containers

Deactivating the container feature allows users to revert to using sections for their website layout. As 10Web Builder is based on Elementor Page Builder, global settings for containers are to be accessed via Elementor tab of your site’s WordPress Admin dashboard. Follow these steps to deactivate containers:

  1. Navigate to your WordPress dashboard and go to Elementor > Settings > Features to find the experimental features tab.
  2. Scroll to locate the Container feature within the list.
  3. In the dropdown menu select Inactive.
  4. A confirmation prompt will appear; click Deactivate to confirm your choice.
  5. At the bottom of the page, click Save Changes to apply your settings.

Consequences of deactivating containers

If you deactivate flexbox containers on sites originally built with sections, there will be no impact on your site content.

For sites created with both sections and containers, content developed using containers won't display. However, reactivating containers will restore access to this content.

Note:

If you generate new content with sections and save the changes without activating Flexbox containers, any content created within containers earlier will be lost.

If your website uses solely containers or both sections and containers, and you deactivate and reactivate the Flexbox containers option without altering the content, your site's content should remain unchanged.

Restoring content after deactivating containers

If you've deactivated Flexbox containers but need to access content created with them again, reactivate Flexbox Containers them via Elementor > Settings > Features.

After doing that navigate to the page where the container content was created. Click on the 10Web Builder logo in the upper left corner and select History > Revisions.

Choose the page version that includes the container content you wish to access and click Apply.

Note:

Applying a previous revision will remove any content added after that revision. If you reactivate containers and apply a revision from a past date, any changes made between that date and the present will be lost.

articles.name: Responsive Editing for Mobile and Tablets with 10Web Website Builder
articles.title: Responsive Editing for Mobile and Tablets with 10Web Website Builder
articles.body:
Creating a website that looks great on all devices - desktops, tablets, and mobiles - is an essential part of web design. 10Web Builder makes this task seamless by providing responsive editing tools.

Understanding responsive design

Responsive design implies adapting your website's layout to the screen size of the device it's being viewed on. The 10Web Builder defines screen sizes as follows: PCs (over 1024px wide), tablets (between 1024px and 767px wide), and mobiles (under 767px wide). Breakpoints are the screen widths at which your site's layout changes to better suit the device's screen size, ensuring your content is always displayed optimally.

Viewing and editing for different devices

To create a responsive website with 10Web Builder, you'll need to follow these steps:

  1. Start editing your page: Open the page you want to customize in the 10Web Builder’s editing tool.
  2. Use the responsive mode: In the top toolbar, you'll find icons for desktop, tablet portrait, and mobile portrait. Click these to see how your site looks on different devices.
  3. Adjust settings for each device: Look for the device icon next to various widget settings when editing each widget. Clicking this lets you switch between device-specific settings. For example, you might change the font size for a heading on mobile devices without affecting its appearance on desktop or tablets.
  4. Review and publish your changes: Once you’re done with editing, you can preview your changes and save them by clicking the Preview changes and Save & Publish buttons in the top right corner of the top toolbar.

Customizing breakpoints

While the 10Web Builder comes with default breakpoints, you might need to customize these or add new ones for greater flexibility:

  1. Access Site Settings from the toolbar: This is where breakpoints can be managed.
  2. Navigate to Layout settings and find the Breakpoints menu: Here, you can view and adjust the default breakpoints.
  3. Add or customize breakpoints: You can add new breakpoints to cater to a wider range of devices or edit existing ones.

Responsive options in advanced settings

10Web Website Builder provides a visual way to identify which settings have device-specific customization. Look for the device icon next to various settings. If the icon is present, you can set different values for desktop, tablet, and mobile views.

Note:

Not all settings offer this level of responsive control. For example, certain widgets or properties within containers may not allow you to directly modify their core behavior for each screen size. In such cases, the device icon may be absent.

To achieve greater customization in these situations, utilize the responsive options found in the Advanced Settings section of widgets and containers. Here's how:

  1. Duplicate and hide: Create two instances of the same widget or container. In the Advanced Settings, set the visibility of one to Hide on Desktop, Hide on Tablet Portrait and Hide on Mobile Portrait. You can customize this for the specific views you'd like.
  2. Customize for each view: Now, with the widgets/containers selectively visible, you have full control to modify their settings and create tailored experiences for each device view.

Important:

This technique provides more granular control over responsive behavior but may increase the complexity of your website structure. Use it strategically when simpler responsive adjustments don't achieve the desired results.

Responsive editing best practices

The practice of responsive web design entails adhering to best practices to guarantee an aesthetically pleasing layout across all devices. Here are two key principles to consider:

  1. Start from the broadest device: Make changes to wider devices first, as these will affect narrower devices. This top-down approach ensures consistency across devices.
  2. Preview changes across all devices: Regularly switch between device views to ensure your edits provide the best user experience on every screen size.

By leveraging the responsive editing features of the 10Web Website Builder, you can ensure your website is engaging and accessible to all visitors, regardless of the device they use to browse your site.

articles.name: How to Add a Background Image
articles.title: How to Add a Background Image
articles.body:
Background images are an important part of web design, helping to make your site more visually appealing. This guide will show you how to easily add and adjust background images to fit your website's design.

Adding a background image

  1. Log in to your 10Web account
  2. Click on the website you want to modify
  3. Click on the edit icon on your website thumbnail or
    Click on AI Builder > Edit Website
  4. Click on the section you need to edit
  5. Navigate to Style > Background type
  6. Click on Classic
  7. Click on the image field to add an image
  8. Adjust the settings as needed

You can choose to add a scrolling and mouse effect by enabling the toggle and adjusting the settings.

Background image options

The designated space for your image is a set box or a grid. Often, images don't align perfectly within this box or grid. However, there is a range of options to fine-tune how your image aligns or fits within this space.

Image resolution

Explore the range of sizes available, starting with a thumbnail and ending with full, and use the one that best suits your design.

Position

  • Larger images: The position setting determines which segment of the image is displayed allowing you to shift and decide which part of the image is seen through the window.
  • For smaller images: This setting dictates where the image will sit within the space. There are pre - set options you can choose from or choose custom. Opting for custom activates sliders, enabling precision adjustments to the image's x and y coordinates.

Attachment

  • Default: Ensures that the image moves along with the content as you scroll. In other words, the element scrolls with the rest of the page.
  • Scroll: Forces the image to stay fixed in the position relative to the viewport, but it does move with the rest of the content when the user scrolls.
  • Fix: Ensures the image remains in a fixed position on the screen regardless of scrolling.

Repeat

If an image is too small for the designated space, it will, by default, repeat to fill the entirety of the space. Choose from these options:

  • No-repeat: Ensures the image is displayed just once.
  • Repeat-x: Stretches the image horizontally.
  • Repeat-y: Let the image extend vertically.

Display size

This feature determines how the image conforms to the space it is in. 

  • Cover: Makes the image take up the whole space, cropping if oversized or enlarging if undersized.
  • Contain: Fits the full image inside the frame, maintaining its proportions, which can sometimes result in blank areas around the image.
  • Custom: Offers a slider to manually adjust the image's width, with the height adjusting proportionately.

Note:

For optimal results, we recommend that you select images tailored to your design's dimensions.

articles.name: Measurement Types
articles.title: Measurement Types
articles.body:
10Web Website Builder offers various units of measurement for sizing elements, with options like PX, EM, REM, %, VW, and VH. Understanding what these units mean and their appropriate application is crucial for responsive and accessible design.

Absolute vs. Relative

Absolute measurements refer to values that are not subject to any restrictions or conditions, providing an unchanging standard for comparison. On the other hand, relative measurements depend on specific contexts, references, or conditions, and they may vary based on changing circumstances.

Absolute units

  • PX: Pixels are fixed units on a given device, but they can be influenced by device resolution. They are practical for elements that require consistent sizing but can pose challenges for responsive design. Pixels are ideal for elements that do not require resizing.

Relative units

  • EM: This unit is dependent on the parent element.
  • REM: Relative to the root (HTML) element.
  • %: A percentage relative to the size of the parent element.
  • VW (viewport width): A viewport width unit, relative to the width of the viewport.
  • VH (viewport height): A viewport height unit, relative to the height of the viewport.

Relative units adapt to different screen sizes and parent element sizes, making them ideal for responsive and fluid layouts.

EM and REM explained

  • EM: Sizes are calculated based on the parent element's font size, which can lead to unexpected sizes when nesting elements.
  • REM: Sizes are calculated based on the root element's size, providing consistency regardless of parent sizing.

%, VW, and VH explained

These units are typically used for layout dimensions like margins, padding, width, and height. For example, using % for column widths ensures responsive adjustments, while VW and VH can create elements that fill the entire viewport's width or height.

Measurement type and their uses

  • Use PX for precise, fixed dimensions.
  • Use EM for scaling related to the parent element’s font size.
  • Use REM for consistent scaling relative to the root element.
  • Use VW/VH for dimensions that respond to the viewport's size.
  • Use % for relative sizing to the parent element’s dimensions.

To change the measurement type, check this article.

articles.name: How to Organize Elements in a Flexbox Container
articles.title: How to Organize Elements in a Flexbox Container
articles.body:
Containers in 10Web Website Builder allot exceptional flexibility when it comes to positioning elements within them. Navigate to the Items section under the Layout tab to access these controls.

Direction

The Direction setting lets you decide the arrangement in which the elements within your container will be showcased.

  • Row: Elements are oriented horizontally.
  • Column: Elements stand vertically.
  • Row-reversed: Elements are displayed horizontally but in the opposite sequence.
  • Column-reversed: Elements are set vertically, but the order is inverted.

Justify content

  • Start: Elements align to the container's beginning or top boundary.
  • Center: Central alignment of elements within the container.
  • End: Elements are positioned at the container's end or bottom boundary.
  • Space Between: Uniform spacing throughout the container, starting with the first item and concluding with the last.
  • Space Around: Equal gaps are maintained both among the elements and between the initial, and final items and the container boundaries.
  • Space Evenly: Uniform spacing is ensured between elements and the container's edges.

Align items

Align Items aids in determining the alignment of elements on their central axis, based on the choice made in the Direction option.

  • Start: Elements align at the container's left.
  • Center: Elements centrally align within the container.
  • End: Elements position at the container's right.
  • Stretch: Elements expand to span the entire container width or height.

Elements gap

Here, you can adjust the spacing between individual elements, be it widgets or other containers. The units available are pixels (PX), percentages (%), or Viewport Width (VW).

Note:

The default gap between elements is 20PX. However, this can be modified by heading to Site Settings > Layout.

Wrap

The Wrap feature determines if the elements inside will stay confined to a single row or if they overflow to subsequent rows.

  • No Wrap: All elements are constrained to a single horizontal line.
  • Wrap: If items exceed the container's width, they transition to the next line.

Note:

Dive deeper into options related to organizing elements within containers by checking out the Advanced tab.

What’s next

Now armed with insights on organizing widgets within a container, immerse yourself in the intricate settings available under the Layout tab.

articles.name: How to Add a Gradient Background
articles.title: How to Add a Gradient Background
articles.body:
A gradient background can add depth and perspective to a website by combining two colors that blend into one another.

Adding a gradient background

To add a gradient background: 

    1. Select the container you want to modify within your canvas.
    2. From the left-hand settings panel, navigate to Style > Background Type.
    3. Click the Gradient icon to access Gradient Settings.
    4. Click the color tile to set the first gradient color under Color.
    5. Under Location, use the slider to adjust the color spread.

      Note:

      Location determines where each of the colors will start to fade.

    6. Set the second gradient color under the Second color.
    7. Adjust the location of the second color to control its spread.
    8. Choose the type of gradient: Linear or Radial.

If you choose Linear: Set the gradient angle to determine the orientation of the color blend. 

If you choose Radial: Select the position from which the color blend should radiate.

Lastly, you can also add Vertical, Horizontal, Transparent, Blur, and Scaling scrolling effects.

articles.name: How to Create a Flexbox Container
articles.title: How to Create a Flexbox Container
articles.body:
10Web Website Builder’s containers are fundamental for organizing web page elements and structuring your layout efficiently. If you have generated or converted a website using the 10Web AI Builder, then the Flexbox container feature is activated on your website.

How to create containers

articles.name: How to Add a Video Background
articles.title: How to Add a Video Background
articles.body:

Adding a video background

To use a video as a background:

  2. Click on a section or a container
  3. Go to the Style tab

Setting up your video background

articles.name: Container Style Tab Options
articles.title: Container Style Tab Options
articles.body:
Navigate the container style tab to customize the visual presentation of items within a container.

Background settings

  • Background Type: Choose the desired background type: classic, gradient, video, or slideshow.
  • Color (background): Utilize the color picker to define the hue for your background.

    Image Resolution: Controls the display size of the image (thumbnail, full size, or a custom size you choose).

articles.name: How to Save and Reuse Flexbox Containers
articles.title: How to Save and Reuse Flexbox Containers
articles.body:
Containers play a key role in web design, as they hold widgets and other containers, allowing you to build complex layouts. By saving these layouts as templates, you can easily reuse them across projects in Elementor, making your workflow more efficient and speeding up the creation of visually appealing websites.

How to duplicate a container

How to save a container

  4. Click Save

articles.name: Flexbox Advanced Tab Configuration
articles.title: Flexbox Advanced Tab Configuration
articles.body:
In the 10Web Website Builder, the Advanced tab is your gateway to an array of options that further refine the design and layout of your containers.

Margin

Margin defines the external space around the element, adjustable in PX, EM, %, REM, and VW. You can unlink these values for individual side adjustments by clicking the chain icon.

Padding

Padding sets the internal space within the element, with values in PX, EM, %, REM, and VW. The chain icon allows for individual side customization.

Width (Widgets only)

The width determines the horizontal space an element takes up.

Default: The element uses the default width behavior specified in the plugin settings or inherits the width from the theme's styling rules

Full Width (100%): The element stretches across the full width of its container.

Inline (auto): The element takes up only as much space as needed.

Custom: You can define a specific width using the slider or input fields in PX, %, or VW.

Note:

The Inline (auto) setting is not applicable to Containers, which instead relies on the Container's Direction property.

Align Self

This property allows you to override the container’s default alignment for individual items.

Flex-start: Aligns at the start of the container.

Center: Centers in the container.

Flex-end: Aligns at the end of the container.

Stretch: Stretches to fit the container.

Order

Order can be used in responsive design to rearrange elements based on screen size:

Start: Default ordering.

End: Reverses the order.

Custom: Enables manual input for order preference.

Learn about the intricacies of the Order property in our comprehensive guide.

Size

Flex grow/shrink properties define how an element resizes relative to others in the same container:

None: No flex resizing.

Grow: Allows the element to grow.

Shrink: Allows the element to shrink.

Custom: Specify values for flex-grow and shrink manually.

Detailed insights into the Size property are available in our specialized resource.

Position

This setting is for precise control over the element’s positioning:

Default Position: Follows the normal document flow.

Absolute Position: Positions relative to the nearest positioned ancestor.

Fixed Position: Remains fixed within the viewport during scroll.

With Fixed and Absolute positions use the options:

Horizontal Orientation: Defines how the element should be positioned horizontally.

Vertical Orientation: Specifies how the element should be positioned vertically.

Note:

The sticky scrolling effect allows an element to remain in place during scroll but within the confines of its parent section. In contrast, Fixed positioning keeps an element stationary relative to the browser's viewport, regardless of scrolling.

Z-Index

Manipulate the stacking order of elements with the Z-Index; higher values bring elements to the front over lower values.

CSS ID & Classes

Assign unique CSS IDs for scripting or anchor linking and CSS Classes for applying specific style rules.

Important:

Do not apply “#” before the CSS ID and “.“ CSS classes.

articles.name: How to Use 10Web Migration Assistant
articles.title: How to Use 10Web Migration Assistant
articles.body:
The Migration Assistant is a tool aimed at ensuring a smooth, swift, and secure migration of your website using a backup ZIP file. We have transitioned to this advanced and more comfortable migration process to streamline efficiency and convenience.

In the case that the automatic migration of your website has failed, you will be guided by our Migration Assistant to migrate your website using a backup zip file.

Automatic migration failure

Upon the failure of automatic migration, the Migration assistant will pop up and you will see the following warning: “ Something on your website is preventing automated migration.” You will be prompted to migrate your website using a backup zip file of your website.

To make a zip file of your website for migration, you will need to export your website's wp-content folder and the database sql file onto your desktop, make a zip file, then upload the zip file to 10Web. Below are the detailed instructions of this process. 

How to export your wp-content folder

To export your website data, you will need to connect to your website files and folders. 

  1. Log into your hosting provider account
  2. Connect to your website files via your choice of protocol to get started

    For example purposes, we will use an FTP client to export the wp-content folder.

    Note:

    If you don't have access to credentials for connecting to your website files, contact your hosting provider for assistance. If you don’t have access to website files, you can backup your entire website then extract the wp-content folder from the backup.

  3. Onced signed in, locate your wp-content folder 
  4. Export the wp-content folder to your desktop

How to export your database .sql file

You will need to find where your database is located and export it to your desktop as an .sql file. For example purposes we will use PhpMyAdmin. 

To export your .sql file:

  1. Log in to your hosting provider account
  2. Connect your database via PhpMyAdmin

    Note:

    If you don’t have access to the credentials for connection, contact your hosting provider or make a full backup of your website and export the database from the backup.

  3. Once connected, find your database in the left column and click on it

    Note:

    You can find the name of your database in your wp-config file. The name will have the following format: define( 'DB_NAME', 'database_name_here' )

  4. At the top of the PhpMyAdmin page, click on the Export tab
  5. A page with this message will appear: Exporting tables from "name_your database name" database
  6. In the Format section, check that SQL is selected and click Go

An export of your database in .sql format to your desktop will start automatically.

How to create a zip file

You will need to upload both the wp-content folder and the database sql file together as one file. For this reason, you will need to create a zip file which has both the wp-content folder and the .sql file.

Important:

The wp-content folder and the .sql database file should be on the same level.

To create a zip file in Windows:

  1. Select your wp-content folder and the database .sql file
  2. Right click on the selected items
  3. Choose, Compress to Zip file

To create a zip file in Mac OS X

  1. Select your wp-content folder and the database .sql file
  2. Holding Control, click on the selected items
  3. Choose Compress “ Title of your folder”

How to migrate your website using the Migration Assistant

Once you have created a zip file of your website, you can proceed to migrate your website. 

To start migration:

  1. Fill in the subdomain of your website
  2. Choose a data center and click Continue
  3. Fill in your subdomain and choose a datacenter

Note:

If automatic migration has failed, your subdomain and datacenter will be filled in with the information you previously provided.

Once the zip file of your website has been created, you can start the migration process by uploading the zip file. 

Important:

You can upload only zip files. The zip files should not exceed 50GB.

To upload:

  1. Click on Choose a file
  2. Choose the zip file you have created and click Open
  3. Tick the box and agree to allow 10Web to check your files and folders for safety
  4. Click Proceed to start upload

Once your file has uploaded to 10Web, migration of your website will start automatically. 

Important:

articles.name: Troubleshooting Failed Actions in 10Web Dashboard
articles.title: Troubleshooting Failed Actions in 10Web Dashboard
articles.body:
10Web Dashboard is an all-in-one tool that simplifies managing and automating various functions of your websites when they are hosted at 10Web or connected via plugins like Speed Booster or the 10Web Manager.

Depending on your subscription plan and status of your sites (hosted/connected), you can perform actions such as:

  • Updating your plugins, themes, WordPress, etc.
  • Activating, deactivating, and deleting plugins and themes
  • Enabling 10Web services 

However, there may be times when certain actions fail, and you receive error messages within the dashboard. Here is a list of the main reasons for the actions in 10Web dashboard to fail.

  • Website is in maintenance mode 
  • REST route is blocked
  • Lost website connection

Below are steps to troubleshoot these issues: 

Step 1: Check if the website is down or has a fatal error

There are several tools available to check if a site is down, such as Down for Everyone or Just Me. Just enter your URL to see the website's status. This way you can determine if the website is accessible through the internet. 

Step 2: Check if the website is in maintenance mode

If your website is in maintenance mode - be it a default WordPress one or a plugin-induced one - dashboard functions may also be obstructed. Make sure to disable maintenance mode before proceeding with 10Web Dashboard steps again. You can find the complete maintenance mode troubleshooting article here. 

In case your website is available through the internet and is not in maintenance mode, please, proceed with the below steps. 

If website is not hosted at 10Web

For websites connected to the 10Web dashboard via Speed Booster or 10Web Manager, please try to disconnect the site and connect it again:

Note:

Before proceeding with the steps below, ensure you are using the latest version of the 10Web Booster or 10Web Manager plugin. If an update is available in the Plugins section of your WordPress dashboard, kindly update the plugin to the latest version.

Reconnecting a site via 10Web Manager

  1. Enter Wordpress admin dashboard of your connected site
  2. Navigate to 10Web Manager on the left menu
  3. Find the Disconnect from 10Web Manager button and click it
  4. Connect the site again from the same menu

If the connection is successful, you will be redirected to your 10Web dashboard. 

Reconnecting a site via 10Web Booster

Important:

If you are using Cloudflare CDN, please make sure to revert the root domain A records back to origin server IP before disconnecting your site from 10Web dashboard, otherwise you can experience downtime.

  1. Enter Wordpress admin dashboard of your connected site
  2. Navigate to 10Web Speed Booster on the left menu
  3. Find the Disconnect button
  4. Connect the site again from the same menu

If the connection is successful, you will be redirected to your 10Web dashboard. 

Important:

If you still can’t connect, then you may have issues with REST API or permissions.

If website is hosted at 10Web

If your website is hosted by 10Web, and certain actions are failing, follow these steps to troubleshoot the problem:

Step 1: Check for fatal errors

If your website is facing a critical error on any of the pages, you can find the source of the problem by checking the error logs. Here’s how to do that from your 10Web dashboard:

  1. Log in to your 10Web dashboard and select the website experiencing the error.
  2. Go to Hosting Services > Logs.
  3. In the drop-down menu, select PHP-FPM.LOG.
  4. Look for lines that start with PHP Fatal Error. These lines often contain the name of the plugin or theme causing the issue, with a file path like:
    • wp-content/plugins/[plugin-name]
    • wp-content/themes/[theme-name]

Once you've identified the faulty plugin or theme, you can proceed to deactivate it using SFTP.

Note:

If the error is due to a low memory limit, you may see a fatal error in the logs similar to: "Allowed memory size of X bytes exhausted (tried to allocate X bytes) in /path/to/script." To resolve this, you can increase the memory limit by navigating to Hosting Services > Tools > Advanced settings in your 10Web dashboard.

Step 2: Check domain pointing

If you are using a domain from a third-party registrar, ensure it is correctly pointed to your website. Use a DNS checker to verify that the A record of your root domain resolves to the correct IPv4 address, or check that your domain is using 10Web nameservers.

Important:

If your domain uses Cloudflare with proxies enabled, this may block domain pointing. Temporarily disable the proxy status for the root domain’s A record by setting it to "DNS only" for 5–10 minutes. Once the dashboard services work again, you can re-enable the proxies.

Step 3: Verify wordPress login token

If clicking the W icon in 10Web dashboard leads you to the standard WordPress login screen rather than your admin dashboard, there may be a connectivity issue. Contact 10Web's Customer Care for assistance.

Step 4: Disable security plugins

Security plugins installed on your site could be blocking the REST API, which is necessary for some hosting services. Try temporarily disabling these plugins to see if the issue is resolved.

Step 5: Contact support

If none of the above steps resolve the issue, feel free to contact 10Web support team for further assistance. We are available 24/7 to help.

articles.name: Can I Use 10Web Builder With Elementor Pro
articles.title: Can I Use 10Web Builder With Elementor Pro
articles.body:
10Web Builder and Elementor Pro are designed to work alongside each other on your website. While 10Web Builder is based on Elementor, it operates as an independent plugin with a distinct architecture. This allows you to:

  • Utilize widgets from both plugins on a single webpage. 
  • Apply Elementor Pro templates to websites created with 10Web Builder

    Important:

    Applying Elementor Pro Templates to websites created with 10Web Builder might lead to some unexpected styling conflicts.

  • View Elementor Pro widgets in 10Web Builder interface 

Important:

If you have built your website using both 10Web Builder and Elementor Pro, there are a few risks you should take into consideration in case you decide to deactivate one of the above-mentioned plugins.

Here are key considerations for seamless integration:

Deactivation risks

Functionality loss: Deactivating either plugin will disable specific widgets and features native to that platform.

Template inaccessibility: Deactivating 10Web Builder or Elementor Pro will render templates created in the respective plugin unusable until reactivation.

Data persistence

Form data: Should you deactivate 10Web Builder or Elementor Pro, forms created via 10Web’s Form Maker or Elementor’s Forms become temporarily inaccessible. Submission data collected will be retained in all cases. Reactivation will restore the forms.

Tips 

Widget Compatibility: Prior to deactivation, audit your website to identify dependencies on widgets from either plugin.

Debugging: If you encounter widget issues, examine both 10Web Builder and Elementor Pro settings to isolate the root cause.

By paying attention to these specifics, you can efficiently utilize both 10Web Builder and Elementor Pro, maximizing your website’s functionality and design capabilities.

articles.name: My Website Doesn’t Open: How Do I Fix an NXDOMAIN Error?
articles.title: My Website Doesn’t Open: How Do I Fix an NXDOMAIN Error?
articles.body:
Encountering an error message like Error dns_probe_finished_nxdomain or This site can't be reached - Server IP address could not be found when trying to open your website? These types of errors occur when DNS isn't resolving correctly to the domain name or the hosting server's IP address. Depending on your operating system and browser, you may see a different error message such as:

  • Chrome: This site can't be reached. Server IP address could not be found. DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN
  • Firefox: Hmm. We're having trouble finding that site. We can't connect to the server.
  • Edge: Hmmm… can't reach this page. Make sure you've got the right web address.
  • Safari: Safari can't find the server. Safari can't open the page because Safari can't find the server.

This is often due to:

  • Incorrect DNS records
  • A connection issue with your device or network
  • Misspelling the domain name in the browser address bar
  • A firewall, antivirus, or VPN interfering with access to the website
  • The domain is unregistered or expired

Generally, to resolve these types of DNS errors:

  • If you have recently pointed a domain, or made changes to DNS records, confirm the new records are entered correctly.
  • Clear the browser cache
  • Flush your computer's DNS cache

To troubleshoot these types of errors after pointing your domain, first check to see if the DNS records were entered correctly.

How to verify DNS records were added properly

When you point a domain, you usually enter your web host’s nameservers or an A record in the domain’s DNS records. You can use tools like What'sMyDNS to verify that the A record or nameservers were added properly.

If you have used an A record to point a domain to 10Web

  1. Enter your domain and select A from the drop down menu.
  2. The domain’s A record should match the IPv4 address found in your 10Web dashboard's Datacenter & IP section located under Hosting Services > Credentials.
  3. If the A record isn't showing up right, you should correctly point your domain to 10Web.

If you have used nameservers to point a domain to 10Web

  1. Enter your domain and select NS from the drop down menu.
  2. The nameservers shown in What'sMyDNS should match your 10Web nameservers. Go to Domains and click Details to view the Nameservers section and confirm they are correct.
  3. If the nameservers aren't showing up right, you should correctly point your domain to 10Web.

What to do if DNS records are configured properly 

Different caching layers can retain data that may affect your ability to access or view a website. If you recently changed the domain’s DNS records, and you confirmed that the new records are entered correctly, but you’re still getting errors, here are some things you can do to troubleshoot the issue.

Quick tip:

Restarting your computer and router often fixes errors like Error dns_probe_finished_nxdomain or This site can’t be reached.

Browser cache

Clear the cache in Chrome:

  1. Click the 3 vertical dot menu in the upper right corner
  2. Hover over More tools
  3. Click Clear browsing data
  4. Select the time range to delete data from the cache
  5. Make sure the Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files options are both checked.
  6. Click Clear data

Instead of clearing the browser cache, you can bypass it by checking the site on another device, with a different browser, or in an incognito window.

Chrome DNS cache

Clear Chrome’s DNS cache:

  1. Enter chrome://net-internals/dns address in the address bar
  2. Click DNS
  3. Click Clear host cache
  4. Close the tab to exit

Flush the network cache and renew the computer’s IP address

In some cases, you may not see the changes to DNS because of a network cache. To confirm everything is working correctly, please use a different internet connection or see our article for step-by-step instructions on flushing the network cache.

Temporarily disable any antivirus or VPN

Antivirus software and VPNs can both affect network settings. If you are using any of these types of software or services try temporarily disabling them to see if it gets rid of the nxdomain error.

articles.name: How Do I Fix a 403 Forbidden Error?
articles.title: How Do I Fix a 403 Forbidden Error?
articles.body:
Wondering how to fix a 403 forbidden error? It's usually due to a missing index.php file. Here's how you can resolve it:

Creating a new index.php file in FileZilla

  1. You can directly access the Filezila FTP client website using this link: https://filezilla-project.org/. Use an FTP client like FileZilla to access your website files.
  2. Navigate to the folder /home/wplive/web/wp-live.
  3. Verify that the index.php file is there.
  4. If it’s not there, create a new index.php file by right-clicking in the list of files and selecting Create new file.
  5. Right-click the new index.php file and select View/Edit to open it in a text editor (If the file doesn't open automatically, use the pop-up prompt and select notepad.exe from C:\Windows\System32 to open it.)
  6. Copy and paste the following code snippet in index.php.
     
    <?php
/**
 * Front to the WordPress application. This file doesn't do anything, but loads
 * wp-blog-header.php which does and tells WordPress to load the theme.
 *
 * @package WordPress
 */

/**
 * Tells WordPress to load the WordPress theme and output it.
 *
 * @var bool
 */
define( 'WP_USE_THEMES', true );

/** Loads the WordPress Environment and Template */
require __DIR__ . '/wp-blog-header.php';
  7. Save, and close the text editor.

Creating and uploading index.php from your computer

If you're having trouble creating a new index.php file in FileZilla, try creating the file locally, then upload it to /home/wplive/web/wp-live. Here's how to do that in Windows:

  1. Open a File Explorer window and use the right click menu to create a new text file.
  2. Double click the new text file to open it in Notepad.
  3. Add the code snippet above.
  4. Save and exit the text editor.
  5. Using FileZilla, upload the new file by dragging it from the File Explorer window to the /home/wplive/web/wp-live folder.
  6. Right-click on the new file in FileZilla and rename it to index.php. 

If index.php already exists

If the index.php file is already present, please contact customer care for help.
